text:
incident-bot: [P1] GPU saturation — us-west-2-prod. symptom: inference queue >15k, tail latency spiking, autoscaler not reacting. custom metrics for HPA show stale/no data. Paging @kai (oncall-runtime).

kai (oncall-runtime): on it. I can see long queue on router, many requests in Pending state. HPA target metric (inference_queue_length) reads 'no data'.

rachel (oncall-infra): checking prometheus-adapter and metrics-server. prom-adapter returning 503s: `GET /apis/external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` -> 503. metrics-server looks healthy.

diego (sre-lead): if adapter is failing HPA won't get external metrics. Live mitigation options: (1) restart adapter, (2) create temporary HPA override to use CPU metric, (3) manually scale replicas / bring more GPU nodes. Prioritize bringing capacity online.

em (ml-runtime): manual scaling is tricky — most pods end up Pending if nodes lack GPU. We have a small fallback nodepool (gpu-surge) with spare capacity but it's in scale-to-zero mode. Rachel, can you spin it up?

rachel (oncall-infra): gpu-surge pool min=0 due to cost optimization. I can set min=2 and request fast provisioning. Doing: `aws autoscaling update-auto-scaling-group --auto-scaling-group-name gpu-surge --min-size 2 --desired-capacity 2`. ETA ~3m to join cluster.

k8s-bot: prometheus-adapter pod prometheus-adapter-7 restarted by kai.

kai (oncall-runtime): restarting prom-adapter now: `kubectl rollout restart deployment prometheus-adapter -n monitoring`

deploy-bot: rollout started for deployment/prometheus-adapter in monitoring.

em (ml-runtime): heads-up — adapter was recently updated to a version with new auth plugin. If RBAC or serviceaccount token is misconfigured it could return 401/403 intermittently and then backoff. Logs?

kai (oncall-runtime): watching logs: `level=error msg="adapter: external metrics request failed: 403 Forbidden: cannot get metrics: token invalid"` then `level=warning msg="backoff retry in 5m"`. Looks like a token expiry + retry/backoff.

diego (sre-lead): ok, adapter restart should pick up a fresh token. Meanwhile, manual temporary workarounds: em, can you patch the inference deployment to add a second (smaller) replica set that runs reduced batch size so it fits on the spare nodes? That will at least reduce queue length while full-capacity pods come up.

em (ml-runtime): creating a scaled-down lighter deployment: `kubectl apply -f inference-lightweight-rs.yaml -n prod` with nodeSelector `gpu-type: t4` that matches gpu-surge. Will route only low-latency customers to it via route rule. Applying now.

kai (oncall-runtime): route rules applied to split traffic; lighter pods receiving ~20% of traffic. Queue dropped from 15k -> 9.2k.

rachel (oncall-infra): gpu-surge nodes joining cluster, NodeReady.

k8s-bot: HPA/inference-hpa reported: external metrics not found.

kai (oncall-runtime): prom-adapter logs now show successful scrape and registration: `registered external metrics: inference_queue_length`

k8s-bot: HPA/inference-hpa changed: TARGETS 60%/100% -> REPLICAS 18 (scaled up).

diego (sre-lead): good. HPA resumed. However noticed HPA maxReplicas=25 and demand would need ~60 at peak. We hit scale limits quickly. Suggest bumping maxReplicas and also increase ASG max for gpu-pool. Rachel can you raise ASG max?

rachel (oncall-infra): ASG max for gpu-pool increased from 10 -> 40. Cloud quota warning submitted; temporary raise approved for 2 hours.

em (ml-runtime): with adapter healthy now HPA is scaling but pods are taking time to schedule while kube-scheduler finds GPU resources. Some pods are Pending due to ptp label mismatch (some nodes tainted for training workloads). I'm patching tolerations to allow inference pods to land on those nodes temporarily.

kai (oncall-runtime): applied toleration patch to inference deployment; new pods scheduled. Queue now 2.1k and trending down.

tess (cs-ops): customers: major tenants saw 429/timeout for ~20 minutes, ticket volumes spiking. Posting status: "Partial outage: inference delays in us-west-2; mitigation in progress."

diego (sre-lead): summary of live actions:
- restarted prometheus-adapter to clear backoff/tokenissue
- temporarily increased gpu-surge pool to get quick capacity
- deployed lightweight inference replica set to offload traffic
- bumped ASG max and allowed HPA to scale up
- applied tolerations to land pods on additional nodes

kai (oncall-runtime): note: the initial root cause appears to be a token refresh bug in prom-adapter combined with overly aggressive backoff. Also process: cost-savings set gpu-surge min=0 and gpu-pool had low max which slowed recovery.

em (ml-runtime): mitigation note: temporarily lowered per-pod batch size and request CPU to fit more pods per node. We'll revert later.

rachel (oncall-infra): follow-ups created: INF-481 adapter token refresh patch + roll (rachel + infra); INF-482 autoscaling policy review (rachel + platform); INF-483 HPA max & routing adjustments (em + diego); INF-484 runbook update for rapid pool provisioning (kai + ops).

tess (cs-ops): drafting customer impact report and targeted messages. ETA 45m.

diego (sre-lead): incident status -> mitigated. Queue stable <500, error rate back to baseline. Handing to post-incident owners diego + em. Kai start post-incident notes in PagerDuty.

kai (oncall-runtime): handing off to night oncall @rachel in 20m. Leaving channel notes.

diego (sre-lead): thanks all. Slack incident closed; will link postmortem here when ready. (reactions: :trophy: :clap: :rotating_light:)
